title: One More Turn
summary: Occupy the center at the end of your turn and keep it through the opponent's next turn.
designQuestion: Does one shared hex create interaction without expanding into area control?
result: P1 wins after nine turns by swapping onto the center and anchoring there.
findings: The delayed score gives each threat a clear response window.
The same push can clear the center or protect an approach.
Anchor is more interesting when it must be timed on a public objective.

config.movementRule: Move one piece, then use one ability.

rules: Move one piece by one hex on your turn.
Control the center when only your piece occupies it.
Score at the start of your next turn if control remains yours.
The first hold scores and wins.

entries.reasoning: Early control forces P2 to interact. P1 accepts that A can be displaced.

actions.note: P1 threatens to score next turn.

entries.summary: P2 swaps A onto the objective.
entries.reasoning: Swap answers the threat and creates a new one with the same action.

actions.note: Take the center and displace its occupant.

entries.summary: B pushes the new controller away from center.
entries.reasoning: P1 clears the threat without occupying the objective. This keeps both pieces flexible.

entries.summary: B enters the center and anchors.
entries.reasoning: P2 invests its defensive ability only after it creates a scoring threat.

entries.summary: A pulls the anchor away, then B takes center.
entries.reasoning: Pull attacks from a different direction than Push. The second piece converts the clearance into a threat.

actions.note: Pull B off center without testing Anchor head-on.

entries.summary: A pushes B off center and B returns behind it.
entries.reasoning: The defender uses both pieces. One clears the hex while the other claims it.

actions.note: Return to center from the side.
P2 creates a third scoring threat.

entries.summary: A swaps onto center and anchors there.
entries.reasoning: P1 combines an offensive swap with defensive resistance. P2 must find a non-push answer.

actions.note: Take center while moving its occupant away.

entries.summary: P2 finds a push line, but Anchor holds.
entries.reasoning: P2 already spent Swap. Its remaining interaction cannot remove the center piece this turn.

entries.summary: P1 begins its turn in control and scores the hold.
entries.reasoning: The win comes from timing Anchor on a scoring threat, not from permanent defense.
